title: Customer Signal Index Builder
body:
Purpose:

This working worksheet defines a lightweight, actionable Customer Signal Index (CSI) that we can compute weekly to power QBRs, renewal risk flags, and playbook triggers. The approach trades bespoke scoring per account for a standardized composite index that is: (a) interpretable by CS reps and AEs, (b) tunable over time, and (c) easy to backfill from existing event, billing and support sources.

High-level design goals:
- Single composite index (0-100) that summarizes multi-dimensional health.
- Signal categories cover adoption, value realization, engagement, financial posture, support friction, and product/fit signals.
- Dynamic weighting rules so we can emphasize different signals for different customer tiers.
- Simple thresholds for green/yellow/red plus signal-specific triggers for playbook actions.

Signal categories and candidate metrics (default weights):
1) Adoption & Usage (weight 28)
   - DAU/MAU for core feature set (normalized 0-100)
   - % of active seats using feature X weekly (normalized)
   - Session length / median tokens per session for inference customers
   Rationale: strongest signal of ongoing value.

2) Value Realization (weight 22)
   - KPI hit rate (customer-defined success metric: % of targets met)
   - New product features adopted in last 90 days (binary -> score)
   - Usage-to-cost ratio (value per token / spend)
   Rationale: shows business impact beyond raw activity.

3) Executive & Stakeholder Engagement (weight 12)
   - Last executive touch (days since) -> recency score
   - Frequency of roadmap alignment meetings past 180 days
   Rationale: exec engagement reduces churn risk at enterprise scale.

4) Financial Signals (weight 18)
   - Days past due on invoices (scaled)
   - Contract renewal horizon (months until renewal normalized)
   - Expansion requests / upsell activity (scaled)
   Rationale: immediate renewal risk and commercial momentum.

5) Support & Reliability Signal (weight 12)
   - Open severity-1/2 incidents in last 30 days (count -> penalty)
   - Mean time to resolution (MTTR) relative to SLA
   - Reopened tickets %
   Rationale: friction and reliability drive fast negative sentiment.

6) Product-fit & Roadmap Alignment (weight 8)
   - % of product gaps reported that are on our roadmap (higher = good)
   - Custom integration progress (milestones completed)
   Rationale: captures strategic fit and implementation momentum.

Scoring & normalization rules (practical):
- Each metric is normalized to a 0-100 scale. Use historical percentiles where sensible (e.g., 0 -> 10th pct, 50 -> 50th pct, etc.). For binary signals (feature adopted), use 0 or 100.
- Category score = average of metrics in the category (or weighted average if we add sub-weights).
- Customer Signal Index (CSI) = round(sum(category_score_i * category_weight_i)/sum(all_weights), 1). Default total weight = 100.

Threshold guidance (tunable):
- CSI >= 75: Green (low renewal risk). Maintain cadence; look for expansion opportunities.
- CSI 50-74: Yellow (monitor). Trigger targeted intervention: identify lowest-scoring categories and assign an owner.
- CSI < 50: Red (high risk). Immediate playbook: exec escalation + technical SWAT + commercial review.

Signal-specific playbook triggers (examples):
- Adoption drop: If adoption category drops >= 20 points week-over-week -> trigger 1:1 with CSM within 3 business days, run a 7-day usage re-onboarding sequence, surface onboarding playbook doc, and propose a low-effort product fix (if applicable). Owner: CSM.
- Financial delinquency: Any invoice past 30 days -> trigger 1: Account ops + AE invoice remediation; 2: Freeze non-critical new seats (per contract). Owner: AE + Rev Ops.
- Repeated sev1 incidents: More than 1 sev1 in 60 days -> trigger tech lead sync + postmortem + credits discussion. Owner: SRE liaison + CSM.
- No exec touch in 180 days for enterprise accounts -> trigger AE executive re-engagement task and standardized exec one-pager. Owner: AE.

Example calculation (sample account "Orchard AI"):
- Adoption: DAU/MAU normalized -> 65; feature coverage -> 80; session length -> 50 => cat avg = 65
- Value realization: KPI hit rate 40, features adopted (1/3 -> 33), value-to-cost ratio 55 => cat avg = 43
- Exec engagement: last touch 210 days -> scaled 10 => cat = 10
- Financial: invoices current (100), renewal in 9 months -> scaled 70, upsell interest 0 -> cat avg = 57
- Support: 1 sev2 open -> penalty -> cat = 40
- Product-fit: roadmap alignment 80 -> cat = 80
CSI = round((65*28 + 43*22 + 10*12 + 57*18 + 40*12 + 80*8)/100, 1) = round((1820 + 946 + 120 + 1026 + 480 + 640)/100, 1) = round(5032/100, 1) = 50.3 -> Yellow (action: CSM playbook + AE executive outreach).

Operational notes / data sources: 
- Event/usage: Mixpanel / Snowflake derived table cs_daily_usage_v2
- Billing: Stripe + NetSuite pipeline (revops sync job)
- Support: Zendesk export + SRE incidents table
- Engagement: Salesforce touchpoints + calendar events (CS -> calendar sync)
- Feature adoption: product instrumentation events + consent versioning

Implementation checklist (MVP runbook):
- [ ] Finalize metric-level normalization params (percentile cutoffs). Owner: Data Analyst (CS)
- [ ] Backfill CSI for last 12 months for top 200 accounts. Owner: Analytics
- [ ] Add CSI to account 360 view in Salesforce. Owner: Platform Integrations
- [ ] Create automated Slack channel alerts for CSI dips > 15 week-over-week for accounts with ARR > $100k. Owner: SRE + CS Tools
- [ ] Draft one-pager playbooks for top 6 triggers. Owner: CSM enablement

Rollout considerations / variants by segment:
- SMB: downweight Exec Engagement to 5 and upweight Adoption to 40; use simplified playbooks focused on onboarding sequences.
- Enterprise: keep default weights but add a gravity factor for contract size (CSI floor cannot be > 10 points above the contract-health heuristic).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we incorporate qualitative sentiment from NPS or CSAT free text via simple sentiment scoring? (Pros: early warning; Cons: noisy).
- How to surface CSI in QBR templates (visuals, top 3 signals to focus on)? Suggest: chart CSI trend, top 3 negative contributors, and a 4-step action plan.

Quick QBR bake-in (suggested slide outline):
1) CSI trend (6/12 months) + current band (G/Y/R)
2) Top 3 weak signals + supporting metrics
3) Proposed intervention + owner + ETA
4) Wins / improvements since last QBR (metrics)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a living worksheet. Please comment with realistic thresholds and missing data sources.
- If you have a customer in mind where this would have flagged risk earlier, add the account name and a brief note so we can validate sensitivity.

References / related docs:
